findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "prompt:check_my_agent_setup" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Have your coding agent read its own permission rules, hooks, skills and sandbox settings, remove every secret, and check them with check_agent_setup against the…

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "registry" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search, get_weekly_calls, related_to · Private data: get_weekly_calls, get_ai_models, check_agent_setup · Public sink: related_to, check_agent_setup · Destructive: check_agent_setup, get_kit.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search, get_weekly_calls, related_to · Private data: get_weekly_calls, get_ai_models, check_agent_setup · Public sink: related_to, check_agent_setup · Destructive: check_agent_setup, get_kit

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
